metadata.description: An outcome: one resource's logs reach a log store, filtered and tagged with the resource's identity. A Base by the Base test (CLS-002): RFC 9742 (the IETF syslog management model), Redfish EventDestination and the OpenTelemetry Collector each treat "send this system's logs to a collector, filtered" as one deliverable, and a host agent, a BMC, a switch or a cluster forwarder can all fill it. The wire protocol is the Type tier (LogShipper.Syslog, LogShipper.OTLP). The mechanism (a configuration-management role, a device setting, a cluster forwarder) is the provider's; swapping it never touches this contract. What is shipped is chosen by a criterion over the log record's fields, the same kind a LogStore uses to decide how long to keep it.

source.description: Which logs: the systemd journal (default), on-disk files, the device's own log (`native`, for appliances, BMCs and switches that send their own syslog), container logs, or audit logs.

filter.description: Which lines to ship, as two criteria over the log record (identifier-scheme §9.7): `include` (absent: every line) and `exclude` (absent: none). A line ships when it matches `include` and not `exclude`. The outcome is what is promised: lines outside the filter never reach the store. A provider whose sender cannot evaluate a criterion (a BMC filters by facility and severity only) filters before the store or refuses at placement; it never stores more than was asked for.

labels.description: Extra resource attributes stamped on every message, named per the OpenTelemetry semantic conventions (`deployment.environment`, `service.name`). The provider always stamps the target's `host.name` and `udlm.handle` itself, so a log line can be followed back to its record.

status.description: Realized health of the shipper (e.g. running / degraded), as reported by discovery.

shipping_to.description: The intake endpoint the shipper is delivering to, resolved from the store's published intake (echo of realized config).

last_shipped_at.description: OBSERVED — a provider-watched liveness fact, not derivable from model records (no shipment-instance records exist; this is heartbeat, not history). Timestamp of the most recent message the store received from this target (RFC 3339) — drives staleness detection.

relationships.name: sink
relationships.description: The log store the logs go to. The shipper binds the store's published `intake_endpoints` output that matches its protocol, so moving the store's receiver changes one record, not every shipper.

relationships.name: host
relationships.description: The machine whose logs are shipped (a VM or a bare-metal host). Exactly one of host, bmc, switch, gateway or cluster is set.

relationships.name: bmc
relationships.description: The baseboard management controller whose own log is shipped (`source` native).

relationships.name: switch
relationships.description: The switch whose own log is shipped (`source` native).

relationships.name: gateway
relationships.description: The gateway whose own log is shipped (`source` native).

relationships.name: cluster
relationships.description: The cluster whose container, node or audit logs are shipped by a cluster-level forwarder.

adopts.standard_name: Semantic conventions (resource attributes) and Logs Data Model
adopts.role: the attribute names in `labels`, the identity the provider stamps (`host.name`), and the log record fields a `filter` criterion addresses

context.purpose: Declares the outcome that a resource's logs reach a log store, without saying anything about how.
context.plain_description: A statement of outcome: logs from one resource (a machine, a BMC, a switch, a gateway or a cluster, named by a `contained_by` edge) reach a log store (the `sink` edge), filtered by `source` and a `filter` criterion, and tagged with the resource's identity. The protocol is chosen by the Type: Syslog or OTLP. The consumer never sees the mechanism; whether a provider satisfies it with an automation-managed agent, a device setting or a cluster forwarder is the provider's business, and swapping mechanisms changes nothing in this record. Realized state reports whether shipping is healthy and when the store last heard from the target, which drives staleness detection.
use_when: You need logs-from-resource-X-land-in-the-store as a declared, checkable fact per resource.
You need shipping health and last-delivery time surfaced for drift and staleness detection.
not_for: The log store itself — that is LogStore; this class binds to it.
Metrics or trace collection — not covered; this class is logs.
works_with: Machine / BMC / NetworkSwitch / NetworkGateway / KubernetesCluster — the resource whose logs are shipped.
LogStore — where the logs go; its published intake is what the shipper binds.
